Hybrid is slow because of the QEMU->vsim state-handoff ceremony, not the simulation. It is a roughly fixed cost (~26s here) that has almost nothing to do with your ROI size, and it never shows up in the cycle figure.

Measured just now on your `hello.elf`:

| run | counted cycles | wall-clock |
|---|---|---|
| `--mode cycle` (whole program on vsim) | 3573 | 0.79s |
| `--mode hybrid` (your run, main->_exit) | 2734 | 27.29s |
| QEMU fast-leg alone (reset->main, drain) | - | **0.08s** |

What this proves:
- The QEMU leg is **0.08s**. Negligible.
- vsim cold-runs the **entire** program (3573 cycles, more than your ROI) in **0.79s**. So simulating everything hello does costs under 1 second.
- The hybrid vsim leg therefore spends `27.29 - 0.08 ~= 27.2s`, of which only ~0.6s is the ROI. The other **~26s is the resume + drain handoff**.

Why the handoff is expensive: `--resume-from-qemu` makes vsim write every GPR/FPR/CSR (and V-state if used) into the **halted** hart through the RISC-V Debug Module (abstract commands + program buffer), and `--handoff-out` reads them all back the same way. Each register access clocks the Verilator RTL through the slow debug-module/JTAG handshake. Those cycles run with the hart halted, so they burn real wall-clock but never advance `mcycle`. That is exactly why you see a tiny cycle number (2734) next to a huge wall time.

When hybrid actually wins: hybrid trades "simulate the pre-ROI region on vsim" for "pay the fixed handoff cost." For hello, the pre-ROI region is only ~839 cycles (3573 - 2734), so you save under 1s of vsim time but pay ~26s of handoff. Net loss. Hybrid only pays off when the part you skip in QEMU (boot, big data load, long warm-up) is **millions+ of cycles** - then skipping it on vsim saves far more than the handoff costs. For a tiny program like hello, use `--mode cycle`.

One side note worth a separate look: a near-empty ROI (`--pc-end 0x100076`) still reported **2728** cycles, basically the same as the full ROI. That suggests the `pc-end` may not be taking effect (likely clamped/ignored), so the cycle figure for very short PC windows may not mean what you expect - but that is a correctness question, separate from the speed one you asked about.

Confirmed: the sim passes **real per-engine caps** (`andes_caps_from_config()`, starts from `none()`), so unimplemented Andes/M-ext CSRs cost **zero** DMI — that path is already optimal. The waste is elsewhere. Here is the full analysis.

## Where the ~26s goes (measured, per-phase)

| phase | time | work |
|---|---|---|
| startup (reset; no ELF load, mmap pre-filled) | ~0.1s | - |
| **RESUME / inject** | **~13.7s** | ~190 DMI register writes |
| ROI execution (main→exit) | ~0.36s | the actual kernel |
| **DRAIN / readback** | **~11.7s** | ~190 DMI register reads |

vsim reports `214505 cycles simulated` but `mcycle` delta is only ~2734 — so **~211k of those cycles are debug-module clocking** that burns wall-clock but never counts. ROI = 0.36s; everything else (25.4s) is the handoff.

## Root cause

Every register crosses the DMI as **one Debug-Module abstract command + a busy-poll loop**. Each costs ~500-1400 simulated cycles, and Verilator runs the whole core model at only ~8 kHz to do it. ~190 registers x 2 directions = ~380 transactions = ~211k cycles = ~25s.

## Needed vs wasted (for scalar `hello`)

| block | inject ops | needed? |
|---|---|---|
| 32 GPR + PC | 32 | yes (live-in) |
| 32 FPR + fcsr | 33 | **wasted** - hello has no FP |
| V sweep + V CSRs | ~74 | **wasted** - hello has no V |
| M trap CSRs, mcache/mmisc, mcycle | ~11 | yes (correctness/cycle-accuracy) |
| Andes + M-ext (caps-gated) | ~42 | yes; **already optimal** |

`flags=0x1f`: FP and V are transported because the **engine has F/V**, not because hello **uses** them. PMP is correctly skipped (M-mode). The whole **drain output is unused unless `--verify` is on** — the driver only reads back `mcycle`.
